triggers: a kernel on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942) risks the '8. q_tile-fast block decomposition wrecks SE load balance on MI308X' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942): 8. q_tile-fast block decomposition wrecks SE load balance on MI308X

problem.statement: Pitfalls: FlyDSL Flash Attention on MI308X (gfx942) -- 8. q_tile-fast block decomposition wrecks SE load balance on MI308X

payload.attempted: a "natural" decomposition of `block_id` is q_tile-fast / head-slow:
payload.lesson: on AMD CDNA3, block scheduling is SE-major then CU-preemptive within each SE. Always put the **uniform-compute** dimension in the fast position of `block_id`, the **non-uniform-compute** dimension (causal q_tile, varying batch lengths) in the slow position.

established_fact.mechanism: MI308X has 16 SEs × 5 CUs and dispatches block_id `i` to SE `i mod 16`. With q_tile-fast, SE 0 gets blocks `{0, 16, 32, ...}` = all the same q_tile of different heads — but for Qwen H_q=16 with 8 q_tiles, SE 0 ends up with all `q_tile=0` (light) blocks, while SE 7 ends up with all `q_tile=7` (heavy) blocks. The pipeline waits for the slowest SE.

payload.observed: 30–76% slower on every Qwen GQA shape than head-fast.
payload.root_cause: MI308X has 16 SEs × 5 CUs and dispatches block_id `i` to SE `i mod 16`. With q_tile-fast, SE 0 gets blocks `{0, 16, 32, ...}` = all the same q_tile of different heads — but for Qwen H_q=16 with 8 q_tiles, SE 0 ends up with all `q_tile=0` (light) blocks, while SE 7 ends up with all `q_tile=7` (heavy) blocks. The pipeline waits for the slowest SE.

implementation.snippet:
```python
q_tile_idx = block_id % num_q_tiles
head_idx   = block_id // num_q_tiles % NUM_HEADS
```
